campaign.name: US Recruitment Camp | Players
campaign.objective: Fill 30 recruitment camp places with ambitious players aged 16 to 21 before registration closes on 23 September.

concepts.name: A Former NBA Player Is Looking For Talent
concepts.strategy: Lead with Dijon Thompson arriving in Birmingham for an active talent search, then make the in-gym assessment the immediate opportunity.
concepts.audience: Ambitious UK basketball players aged 16 to 21 who want their game seen by someone with UCLA, NBA and professional experience.
concepts.proposition: Train and compete in front of Dijon Thompson for a possible opportunity to progress towards the LA trip and US showcase.

ads.primary_text:
A former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player is coming to Birmingham looking for basketball talent.

He’s not coming just to run a session.

He’s looking for players who could get the opportunity to go to LA, train at UCLA and showcase in front of US college and professional coaches.

First, he needs to see you play.

30 players get into the camp.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

If you think you’ve got something, come show him.
ads.headline: A former NBA player is looking for talent.
ads.creative_alt: Dijon Thompson in a Phoenix Suns uniform holding a basketball.

ads.primary_text:
A former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player is coming to Birmingham looking for basketball talent.

That’s Dijon Thompson.

And he’s not coming here just to run a camp and leave.

He’s looking for players.

You’ll train. Get coached. Compete. Let him see your game properly.

Players who stand out could get the opportunity to travel to LA, train at UCLA and showcase in front of college and professional coaches in the US.

Last year, players came through this process and made that trip.

Now he’s back looking again.

We’re only taking 30 players into the camp.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

If you’re 16–21 and think your basketball can go somewhere, come play.
ads.headline: A former NBA player is looking for talent.
ads.creative_alt: Dijon Thompson in a Phoenix Suns uniform holding a basketball.

ads.primary_text:
A former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player is coming to Birmingham looking for basketball talent.

That’s worth understanding properly.

His name is Dijon Thompson.

He played college basketball at UCLA, reached the NBA with Phoenix, then continued his career overseas.

Now he’s coming here to see who can play.

Not from a mixtape.

In the gym.

You’ll train.

Get coached.

Compete.

He gets to see what you do when somebody can actually guard you.

How you make decisions.

How you respond when your first option disappears.

What you do when the shots aren’t falling.

And whether there’s something in your game that could travel.

Because there’s somewhere for this to go.

Players who stand out could get the opportunity to travel to Los Angeles, train at UCLA and showcase in front of college and professional coaches in the US.

Last year, players came through the camp and made that trip.

Now he’s coming back to Birmingham looking again.

We’re only taking 30 players. Enough to create a serious gym, but few enough that the players can actually be seen and assessed.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

You don't need to tell us how serious you are.

Come play.
ads.headline: A former NBA player is looking for talent.
ads.creative_alt: Dijon Thompson in a Phoenix Suns uniform holding a basketball.

concepts.name: Everyone Looks Good In Their Highlights
concepts.strategy: Accept that highlights are useful, then show why a serious evaluator also needs to see the possessions between the clips.
concepts.audience: Players aged 16 to 21 who use highlights to show their game and want a fuller live assessment.
concepts.proposition: Let Dijon see how you defend, decide, compete and contribute when the game is not edited.

ads.primary_text:
Everyone looks good in their highlights.

That’s the point of highlights.

You made the shot. Beat your man. Got the block. Nice.

A former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player is coming to Birmingham because he needs to see the rest.

Can you defend? Make decisions? Compete? Stay useful when you’re not scoring?

30 places.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

Your highlights can introduce you.

Come show him the player.
ads.headline: Your highlights can introduce you.
ads.creative_alt: A basketball player attacks the basket against a defender in live competition.

ads.primary_text:
Everyone looks good in their highlights.

That’s literally the job of the edit.

Made three.

Nice finish.

Big block.

Good.

Now we need the other possessions.

Can you defend?

Do you move the ball?

What happens when somebody takes away your first option?

Can you still have a good game when your shot isn’t falling?

Former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player Dijon Thompson is coming to Birmingham looking for talent he could potentially take to LA and put in front of US college and professional coaches.

So he needs to see you play.

Not just your best bits.

30 players get that opportunity.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

Come show him the rest.
ads.headline: Your highlights can introduce you.
ads.creative_alt: A basketball player attacks the basket against a defender in live competition.

ads.primary_text:
Everyone looks good in their highlights.

That’s what highlights are for.

You made the three.

Beat your defender.

Finished through contact.

Got the block.

Nice.

Keep the clips. They’re useful.

But if somebody is considering taking you to LA and putting your game in front of college and professional coaches, eventually they need the other possessions too.

The one where you don’t touch the ball.

What did you do?

The possession after you turned it over.

Did you get back?

The game where you’ve missed your last four shots.

Are you still helping your team?

Can you guard?

Can you make quick decisions?

What happens when somebody takes away the move that normally works?

That stuff probably isn't making your mixtape.

It still tells us what kind of player you are.

That’s why former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player Dijon Thompson is coming to Birmingham to watch players train and compete.

The players who stand out could get the opportunity to go to LA, train at UCLA and showcase in front of US college and professional coaches.

Only 30 players are getting into the gym.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

Your highlights can introduce you.

Come show him the possessions between them.
ads.headline: Your highlights can introduce you.
ads.creative_alt: A basketball player attacks the basket against a defender in live competition.

concepts.name: Last Year, They Went
concepts.strategy: Use footage from the previous LA and UCLA trip as direct proof that players have already progressed from the recruitment camp to America.
concepts.audience: Players aged 16 to 21 who want tangible evidence of where the recruitment camp can lead.
concepts.proposition: Come through the recruitment camp and compete for the chance to be considered for the next LA group.

ads.primary_text:
Last year, these players came to the recruitment camp.

Then they went here.

UCLA.

They trained, played and got to experience the level for themselves.

Now the former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player who took them there is coming back to Birmingham looking for the next group.

30 places.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

Watch what happened last year.

Then come show him why you should be in the next video.
ads.headline: Last year, they went.
ads.creative_alt: Animated footage from the previous School of Skill trip to Los Angeles and UCLA.

ads.primary_text:
The players in this video came to the recruitment camp last year.

Then they got on a plane to LA.

UCLA.

They trained. Played. Saw the facilities. Got around the programme and experienced the level for themselves.

America stopped being something they watched on a screen.

They were standing in it.

Now former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player Dijon Thompson is coming back to Birmingham looking for the next group.

The camp is where he gets to see you.

Train. Compete. Get coached. Get assessed.

There are 30 places.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

Last year, it was them.

Come show him who should go next.
ads.headline: Last year, they went.
ads.creative_alt: Animated footage from the previous School of Skill trip to Los Angeles and UCLA.

ads.primary_text:
The players in this video came to the recruitment camp last year.

Then they got on a plane to Los Angeles.

UCLA.

And there’s a big difference between saying you want to play basketball in America and actually walking into a place like that.

You see the facilities.

You get around the programme.

You train.

You play.

You see how people work.

You feel what the level is like.

Suddenly, America isn’t basketball on your phone anymore.

You’re standing in it.

For the players who went last year, that changed what they knew was out there.

Now the former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player who helped take them there is coming back to Birmingham looking for the next group.

His name is Dijon Thompson.

He knows UCLA because he played there himself before reaching the NBA and continuing his career overseas.

The recruitment camp is where he gets to see you.

Come in.

Train.

Get coached.

Compete against other good players.

Let him assess your game.

Players who stand out could get the opportunity to make that trip to LA and showcase in front of college and professional coaches.

There are only 30 places in the camp.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

Last year, it was the players you’re watching.

This year?

Come play.

concepts.name: America Comes To Birmingham First
concepts.strategy: Make the distance to US basketball feel practical by bringing an evaluator who played at UCLA and in the NBA into a Birmingham gym.
concepts.audience: Birmingham and West Midlands players aged 16 to 21 who want to pursue basketball opportunities in America.
concepts.proposition: Take a concrete first step from Birmingham by training and competing in front of Dijon Thompson.

ads.primary_text:
Playing basketball in America can feel a long way from Birmingham.

This time, someone who actually did it is coming here.

A former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player is coming to find talent.

Stand out, and you could get the opportunity to go the other way — LA, UCLA, and a showcase in front of US college and professional coaches.

There are 30 places to be seen.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

If America is the plan, get in the gym.
ads.headline: America comes to Birmingham first.
ads.creative_alt: A focused young basketball player stands courtside holding a ball.

ads.primary_text:
A lot of players here want to play basketball in America.

Usually, America is thousands of miles away.

This time, someone who actually played there is coming to Birmingham.

Former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player Dijon Thompson is coming to find talent.

You’ll train.

Get coached.

Compete.

Let him assess your game.

Players who stand out could get the opportunity to travel the other way — to LA, to train at UCLA and showcase in front of college and professional coaches.

Last year, players did exactly that.

This camp has 30 places.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

America is still a long way away.

This is something you can actually do from Birmingham.
ads.headline: America comes to Birmingham first.
ads.creative_alt: A focused young basketball player stands courtside holding a ball.

ads.primary_text:
Playing basketball in America can feel a very long way from Birmingham.

You can train.

Play every weekend.

Put clips online.

Talk about where you want your basketball to go.

But the people and places you’re trying to reach are still thousands of miles away.

This time, someone is coming the other way.

A former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player is coming to Birmingham looking for talent.

His name is Dijon Thompson.

He played at UCLA, reached the NBA and then continued his professional career overseas.

So he has a pretty useful idea of what basketball at another level looks like.

And he’s coming here to watch.

You’ll train.

Get coached.

Compete.

Let him see your game.

The players who stand out could get the opportunity to travel to Los Angeles, train at UCLA and showcase in front of college and professional coaches in the US.

Last year, players made that trip.

This time, there are 30 places in the Birmingham gym.

30 chances to get seen properly.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

Nobody needs a big speech about how badly you want America.

Get in the gym.

Play.

Give someone who’s been there a reason to take a closer look.
ads.headline: America comes to Birmingham first.

concepts.name: Get In A Better Room
concepts.strategy: Show how a serious gym changes what basketball asks from a player and makes strengths and gaps visible quickly.
concepts.audience: Competitive players aged 16 to 21 who want to test themselves alongside other ambitious players.
concepts.proposition: Join a limited 30-player gym with strong competition, coaching and an experienced evaluator watching.

ads.primary_text:
Put good players in a gym together and you find things out pretty quickly.

Someone is quicker than you.

Someone can guard you.

Someone sees a pass you didn’t.

Good.

Now add a former UCLA and NBA player who’s there looking for talent.

That’s a useful room.

We’re putting 30 players in it.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

Come see what your game looks like in there.
ads.headline: Get in a better room.
ads.creative_alt: Two basketball players compete one-on-one while other players watch from the court.

ads.primary_text:
Who you play with changes what basketball asks from you.

Put good players in a gym together and suddenly the easy stuff isn’t so easy.

Someone stays in front of you.

Someone is just as quick.

Someone does something better than you.

Good.

Now you’re finding things out.

That’s the room we’re putting together.

30 young players chasing their basketball seriously.

And a former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player there to coach, watch and assess.

Players who stand out could get the opportunity to go to LA and showcase their game at UCLA in front of US coaches.

But first, get into a good gym.

There are 30 places.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

Come compete.
ads.headline: Get in a better room.
ads.creative_alt: Two basketball players compete one-on-one while other players watch from the court.

ads.primary_text:
You know when you walk into a good gym.

Nobody has to tell you.

The ball moves quicker.

People defend.

You can't sleep through three possessions.

Someone can stay in front of you.

Someone is stronger than the players you normally play.

Someone sees the pass before you do.

Someone does the thing you thought you were really good at a little better than you.

Good.

That’s a useful room.

Because now you’re finding things out about your game.

That’s what we want from this recruitment camp.

30 players who want to see how far their basketball can go.

Training together.

Competing against each other.

Getting coached.

And watching the room is a former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player who has come to Birmingham specifically looking for talent.

That’s Dijon Thompson.

Players who stand out could get the opportunity to travel to LA, train at UCLA and showcase their game in front of college and professional coaches.

So yes, there’s something much bigger that can come from the day.

But you still have to play basketball first.

And there are only 30 places to do it.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

Get in a good room.

Then show us how you look in it.
ads.headline: Get in a better room.
ads.creative_alt: Two basketball players compete one-on-one while other players watch from the court.

concepts.name: We Don't Know Which Player It Is Yet
concepts.strategy: Keep the opportunity genuinely open by acknowledging that the player who stands out may be established, unknown or valuable in ways highlights miss.
concepts.audience: Players aged 16 to 21 who believe their game deserves to be watched properly, whether or not they already have a profile.
concepts.proposition: Enter the 30-player camp and make a live case for consideration for the next LA showcase group.

ads.primary_text:
Someone in this camp could end up at UCLA.

We just don’t know who yet.

That’s why a former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player is coming to Birmingham.

He’s looking for talent.

30 players get the chance to train, compete and be assessed.

The ones who stand out could get the opportunity to showcase in LA.

Registration closes Wednesday 23 September.

We don’t know who he’ll notice yet.

Come make the decision difficult.
ads.headline: We don't know which player it is yet.

ads.primary_text:
Someone in this camp could end up at UCLA.

Right now, we don't know who.

Maybe it’s the player putting up 25 every weekend.

Maybe it’s someone nobody outside their club has heard of yet.

Maybe it’s a player who doesn’t have the best highlights but does a lot of things you only notice when you watch them properly.

That’s why you get players into a gym.

And play.

This time, the person watching is a former UCLA and Phoenix Suns player who’s coming to Birmingham looking for talent.

His name is Dijon Thompson.

He’ll coach.

He’ll watch.

He’ll see how players compete against each other.

And he’ll get a much better idea of what’s actually there.

The players who stand out could get the opportunity to travel to Los Angeles, train at UCLA and showcase their basketball in front of college and professional coaches.

We did it last year.

Players came through the camp and made that trip.

Now there’s another group wondering how far their game could go.

We don't know who’s going to stand out yet.

Come play.
